Kargstaad.name: Kargstaad
Kargstaad.publicNotes:
Frost giants are remorseless marauders who pillage and plunder from those who dare to live near them in desolate, frigid lands. Their clans range from extremely territorial hunters who claim an expanse of tundra and defend it at all costs to nomadic hordes that roam icy slopes in search of settlements to conquer. Frost giant clans are ruled by those who exhibit the greatest ferocity and prowess in battle-massive brutes who proclaim themselves jarl and demand absolute obedience from their followers. If at any time a frost giant wishes to be a jarl, all they must do is issue a challenge to the current jarl and face off in mortal combat, after which the reigning champion continues leading the clan or the victorious challenger assumes control.

Frost giants live in frostbitten realms, and their appearance is reflective of a people weathered and hardened by relentless snowstorms and freezing temperatures. They often wear metal armor adorned with the furs, skin, teeth, and tusks of slain beasts and heft armas as long as dining tables. Their flesh ranges from pale blue to shale gray, and their hair is typically a dingy white or dirty yellow color.

A typical frost giant stands about 15 pies tall and weighs approximately 2,800 pounds.

Giants are massive humanoid criaturas who live in remote regions throughout the world. They are divided into a number of subtypes.

A criatura that fails its save is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Inmovilizado} and takes @Damage[2d6[cold]] daño at the end of each of its turns until it gets free (Escape DC 41).

The giant can't use Chill Breath again for [[/br 1d4 #Recharge Chill Breath]]{1d4 rounds}.

Kargstaad's Giant.name: Kargstaad's Giant
Kargstaad's Giant.publicNotes:
Frost giants are remorseless marauders who pillage and plunder from those who dare to live near them in desolate, frigid lands. Their clans range from extremely territorial hunters who claim an expanse of tundra and defend it at all costs to nomadic hordes that roam icy slopes in search of settlements to conquer. Frost giant clans are ruled by those who exhibit the greatest ferocity and prowess in battle-massive brutes who proclaim themselves jarl and demand absolute obedience from their followers. If at any time a frost giant wishes to be a jarl, all they must do is issue a challenge to the current jarl and face off in mortal combat, after which the reigning champion continues leading the clan or the victorious challenger assumes control.

Frost giants live in frostbitten realms, and their appearance is reflective of a people weathered and hardened by relentless snowstorms and freezing temperatures. They often wear metal armor adorned with the furs, skin, teeth, and tusks of slain beasts and heft armas as long as dining tables. Their flesh ranges from pale blue to shale gray, and their hair is typically a dingy white or dirty yellow color.

A typical frost giant stands about 15 pies tall and weighs approximately 2,800 pounds.

Giants are massive humanoid criaturas who live in remote regions throughout the world. They are divided into a number of subtypes.

Leng Envoy.name: Leng Envoy
Leng Envoy.publicNotes:
Slavers and raiders from the cold, windswept dimension of Leng, these malevolent humanoids range across reality in ominous black ships capable of sailing beyond the borders of dimensions and planes. Although most denizens of Leng seek slaves and plunder like any pirate, others operate as self-styled ambassadors and merchants, sowing discord with far-ranging plots. While the inscrutable denizens dress themselves in flowing robes, veils, and broad turbans to appear human, their aberrant physiology, when glimpsed, is evident from their crown of stubby horns and tentacled jaws to their furry, goat-like legs.

Above the fierce captains who command the infamous black ships are an even higher caste of denizens of Leng. Estos cultists and musicians serve as high priests, laboring to appease the frightening gods who look down upon the Nightmare Realm with cold malice.

Lesser Jabberwock.name: Lesser Jabberwock
Lesser Jabberwock.publicNotes:
Few beasts have inspired as many legends, poems, songs, and myths in as many cultures, as this bizarre draconic criatura. The jabberwock hails from the fey realm of the First World and is part of a group of powerful First World criaturas known collectively as the Tane.

Like all members of the Tane, jabberwocks are living criaturas that age, eat, drink, and sleep, but do not reproduce normally. Instead, they are created directly by the godlike Eldest who rule the First World, and they serve at the pleasure of these capricious and mysterious entities. Believed to be the most powerful of all the Tane, jabberwocks are typically only ever created with one purpose: to wreak destruction and havoc upon the Material Plane. One of the Eldest might send a jabberwock to devastate a country, continent, or even entire world in order to get revenge for some slight made against them by a single mortal. Sometimes, no specific insult or injury is required, as some of the Eldest resent the very existence of the Material Plane and periodically create jabberwocks simply to express the wrath of the First World against its younger and less chaotic sibling.

Once a jabberwock arrives on the Material Plane, its first order of business is to seek out a lair. It prefers dwelling in remote forest locations about a day's flight from civilization-the more dangerous the woodland is to those who might eventually come hunting it, the better!

The relationship between jabberwocks and vorpal armas is the subject of much debate and speculation among scholars, and the various poems, songs, and legends about the jabberwock do little to clarify the issue, conflicting and diverging on this point. Some believe that vorpal armas were first created specifically to combat jabberwocks, but others take the story one step further. They cite evidence in certain ancient myths that there may once have been only a single, unique jabberwock, so powerful that nothing could so much as scratch it-nothing, that is, except for the first vorpal sword, crafted for that very purpose. So epic was the resulting battle that it created strange echoes throughout reality, and as a result, these echoes, in the form of vorpal armas, can now be found on many worlds. Those who subscribe to this belief claim that the jabberwocks seen today are but pale imitations of this proto-jabberwock, and they speculate that only the combined efforts of several Eldest would be sufficient to create such a criatura again.

Variant JabberwocksThe Eldest have sometimes altered certain aspects of the jabberwocks they create. Some of the more notorious or legendario variant jabberwocks include the following.

Frumious Jabberwock: Frumious jabberwocks have two heads. They are level 24 and gain an extra action on each of their turns they can use only to make a jaws Golpe.

Mimsy Jabberwock: Typically hailing from wintry regions of the First World, mimsy jabberwocks have glowing blue-white scales, resist cold instead of fire, and have eyes that burn with blue flames that deal daño de frío instead of daño de fuego.

Slithy Jabberwock: Wreaking destruction beneath the waves, these sinuous and slimy jabberwocks are amphibious, have a swim Velocidad of 80 pies instead of the normal fly Velocidad, and do not have a wing Golpe. A slithy jabberwock's whiffling aura is activated siempre que it swims, makes a tail Golpe, or Burbles.

Lintwerth.publicNotes:
Whining and self-important criaturas, dust mephits are known for their tendency to pronounce doom and gloom at every opportunity, lamenting every insignificant and minor difficulty as though it were an insurmountable obstacle and making themselves out to be heroes for struggling valiantly against their cruel fates. They tend to be thin and gaunt, with dusky brown and gray skin and wings.

Mephits are small, weak criaturas that serve at the whims of other elemental entities. The mephits presented here are less common than air mephits, earth mephits, and the like, as they are a blend of two different elements rather than focusing on one alone.

feat->Composition Spells.name: Conjuros de composición
feat->Composition Spells.description:
Composition Spells

Puedes infuse tu performances with magic to create unique effects called compositions. Compositions are a special type of conjuro that often require tú to use the PERFORMANCE skill when casting them. Composition conjuros are a type of focus conjuro. It costs 1 Focus Point to cast a focus conjuro, and tú start with a focus pool of 1 Focus Point. Tú refill tu focus pool during tu daily preparations, and puedes regain 1 Focus Point by spending 10 minutos using the Refocus activity to perform, write a new composition, or otherwise engage tu muse.

Focus conjuros are automatically heightened to half tu level rounded up, much like cantrips. Focus conjuros don't require conjuro slots, and puedes't cast them using conjuro slots. Taking feats can give tú more focus conjuros and increase the size of tu focus pool, though tu focus pool can never hold more than 3 Focus Points.

Aprendes the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.WILXkjU5Yq3yw10r]{Counter PERFORMANCE} composition conjuro, protecting against auditory and visual effects.

Composition Cantrips

Composition cantrips are special composition conjuros that don't cost Focus Points, so puedes use them as often as tú like. Composition cantrips are in addition to the cantrips tú elige from the occult list. Generally, only feats can give tú more composition cantrips. Unlike other cantrips, puedes't swap out composition cantrips gained from bard feats at a later level, unless tú swap out the specific feat via retraining. Aprendes the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.IAjvwqgiDr3qGYxY]{Courageous Anthem} composition cantrip, which boosts tu allies' attacks, daño, and defense against fear.

feat->Occult Spellcasting.name: Lanzamiento de conjuros ocultistas
feat->Occult Spellcasting.description:
Extraes upon magic from esoteric knowledge. Puedes cast occult conjuros using the Lanzar un conjuro activity, and puedes supply material, somatic, and verbal components when casting conjuros. Because estás a bard, puedes usually play an instrument for conjuros requiring somatic or material components, as long as it takes at least one of tu hands to do so. If tú use an instrument, tú don't need a material component pouch or another hand free. Puedes usually also play an instrument for conjuros requiring verbal components, instead of speaking.

Each day, puedes cast up to two 1st-rank conjuros. Debes know conjuros to cast them, and tú learn them via the conjuro repertoire class feature. The number of conjuros puedes cast each day is called tu conjuro slots.

As tú increase in level as a bard, tu number of conjuros per day increases, as does the highest rank of conjuros puedes cast.

Some of tu conjuros require tú to attempt a conjuro tirada de ataque to see how effective they are, or have tu enemies roll against tu conjuro DC (typically by attempting a tirada de salvación). Since tu key ability is Charisma, tu conjuro tiradas de ataque and conjuro DCs use tu Charisma modifier.

feat->Spell Repertoire (Bard).name: Repertorio de conjuros (bardo)
feat->Spell Repertoire (Bard).description:
The collection of conjuros puedes cast is called tu conjuro repertoire. At 1st level, tú learn two 1st-rank conjuros of tu choice and five cantrips of tu choice. Tú elige these from the common conjuros from the occult conjuro list, or from other occult conjuros to which tienes access. Puedes cast any conjuro in tu conjuro repertoire by using a conjuro slot of an appropriate conjuro rank.

feat->Composition Spells.name: Conjuros de composición
feat->Composition Spells.description:
Composition Spells

Puedes infuse tu performances with magic to create unique effects called compositions. Compositions are a special type of conjuro that often require tú to use the PERFORMANCE skill when casting them. Composition conjuros are a type of focus conjuro. It costs 1 Focus Point to cast a focus conjuro, and tú start with a focus pool of 1 Focus Point. Tú refill tu focus pool during tu daily preparations, and puedes regain 1 Focus Point by spending 10 minutos using the Refocus activity to perform, write a new composition, or otherwise engage tu muse.

Focus conjuros are automatically heightened to half tu level rounded up, much like cantrips. Focus conjuros don't require conjuro slots, and puedes't cast them using conjuro slots. Taking feats can give tú more focus conjuros and increase the size of tu focus pool, though tu focus pool can never hold more than 3 Focus Points.

Aprendes the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.WILXkjU5Yq3yw10r]{Counter PERFORMANCE} composition conjuro, protecting against auditory and visual effects.

Composition Cantrips

Composition cantrips are special composition conjuros that don't cost Focus Points, so puedes use them as often as tú like. Composition cantrips are in addition to the cantrips tú elige from the occult list. Generally, only feats can give tú more composition cantrips. Unlike other cantrips, puedes't swap out composition cantrips gained from bard feats at a later level, unless tú swap out the specific feat via retraining. Aprendes the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.IAjvwqgiDr3qGYxY]{Courageous Anthem} composition cantrip, which boosts tu allies' attacks, daño, and defense against fear.

feat->Occult Spellcasting.description:

Because estás a bard, puedes usually play an instrument for conjuros requiring somatic or material components, as long as it takes at least one of tu hands to do so. If tú use an instrument, tú don't need a material component pouch or another hand free. Puedes usually also play an instrument for conjuros requiring verbal components, instead of speaking.

Each day, puedes cast up to two 1st-rank conjuros. Debes know conjuros to cast them, and tú learn them via the conjuro repertoire class feature. The number of conjuros puedes cast each day is called tu conjuro slots.

As tú increase in level as a bard, tu number of conjuros per day increases, as does the highest rank of conjuros puedes cast.

Some of tu conjuros require tú to attempt a conjuro tirada de ataque to see how effective they are, or have tu enemies roll against tu conjuro DC (typically by attempting a tirada de salvación). Since tu key ability is Charisma, tu conjuro tiradas de ataque and conjuro DCs use tu Charisma modifier.

Tú elige these from the common conjuros from the occult conjuro list, or from other occult conjuros to which tienes access. Puedes cast any conjuro in tu conjuro repertoire by using a conjuro slot of an appropriate conjuro rank.

Tú add to this conjuro repertoire as tú increase in level. Each time tú get a conjuro slot, tú add a conjuro of the same rank to tu conjuro repertoire. At 2nd level, tú select another 1st-rank conjuro; at 3rd level, tú select two 2nd-rank conjuros, and so on. Though obtienes them at the same rate, tu conjuro slots and the conjuros in tu conjuro repertoire are separate. If a feat or other ability adds a conjuro to tu conjuro repertoire, it wouldn't give tú another conjuro slot, and vice versa.

Swapping Spells in tu Repertoire

As obtienes new conjuros in tu conjuro repertoire, tú might want to replace some of the conjuros tú previously learned. Each time obtienes a level and learn new conjuros, puedes swap out one of tu old conjuros for a different conjuro of the same rank. Este conjuro can be a cantrip. Puedes also swap out conjuros by retraining during downtime.

feat->Signature Spells.name: Conjuros de signatura
feat->Signature Spells.description:
Experience enables tú to cast some conjuros more flexibly.

For each conjuro rank tienes access to, elige one conjuro of that rank to be a signature conjuro. Tú don't need to learn heightened versions of signature conjuros separately; instead, puedes heighten these conjuros freely. If has learned a signature conjuro at a higher level than its minimum, puedes also cast all its lower-rank versions without learning those separately. If tú swap out a signature conjuro, puedes replace it with any conjuro tú could have chosen when tú first selected it (i.e., of the same conjuro rank or lower).

Puedes also retrain specifically to change a signature conjuro to a different conjuro of that rank without swapping any conjuros; this takes as much time as retraining a conjuro normally does.

Lizardfolk Warrior.name: Lizardfolk Warrior
Lizardfolk Warrior.publicNotes:
Cuando human scholars speak de antiguo civilizations, ellos usually turn su focus a themselves, researching y lecturing en el first human empires. Cuando ellos drift a others, ellos invariably look a cultures que had conflicts o alliances con antiguo humanity. That el culture de el people called lizardfolk often gets ignored o forgotten even by well-meaning researchers es thus no surprise, but a el lizardfolk themselves ello es no matter. They know su history y value su integrity y privacy-si younger ancestries like humanity aren't interested en learning de lizardfolk empires dating back a before el first human knocked two rocks together a make su first campfire, que's fine con them.

El word 'lizardfolk' es un excellent example de humanity's narrow-sighted view de este culture. El name de su people es 'iruxi', but these reptilian humanoides tienen patiently y good-naturedly accepted el name 'lizardfolk' as un variant, y ellos generally resist urges a call humans y otro mammalians similarly derivative names en return. Iruxis dwell y thrive en todos tropical y temperate biomes, but ellos son most at home en swamplands, coastal regions, y riverlands, for ellos son talented swimmers, y fish y aquatic plantas make up un grande part de su preferred diets.

Efecto The religious symbol of Yhidothrus glows green on the door, sealing it shut while simultaneously shrieking like a tormented soul. Este howl is audible in areas D1-D4 and is loud enough in area D2 to rouse the bodaks.

While the door remains locked, a @Check[athletics|dc:32] check can Force it Open, or a @Check[thievery|dc:32] check can Pick the Lock. The lock can also be removed with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (5th rank, counteract DC 29).

Once triggered, the alarm continues to shriek and the door remains locked until the hazard is disabled or the door is destroyed or opened. Tracing Yhidothrus's hourglass-shaped religious symbol on either side of the door with a fingertip disables the alarm and the locking ward.

Mandragora Swarm.name: Mandragora Swarm
Mandragora Swarm.publicNotes:
A mandragora looks like a freshly pulled tuber that has grown into the malformed shape of a child with a grotesque face and hideously bloated body. Estos insidious little plants typically form when a mandrake root is watered with a demon's blood. Upon absorbing the otherworldly properties of the demon's blood, the root animates and is forced to seek out blood to feast from, lest it die of thirst.

Always famished and in search for sustenance, mandragoras live haunted, pained lives and perform vile and desperate acts to acquire the blood they crave. While they prefer magically infused blood such as that of unicorns, fey, or sorcerers, and they can also feed off of potions, alchemical bombs, and other magical elixirs, a mandragora can subsist on the blood of non-magical criaturas. They find the flavor of mundane blood to be bland and bitter, and they do not blanch at voicing these complaints to the criaturas from which they drink.

While the typical mandragora is the size of a human child, some of these evil plants continue to grow and grow, reaching sizes more comparable to those of giants. Sometimes as they grow, they form additional limbs or rudimentary faces, eventually transforming into truly hideous mockeries of the human form.

Lean and athirst, the hounds of Tindalos are drawn to those who tamper with the flow of time, travel through time, or use magic or rare alchemical drugs to send their thoughts or perception back or forward in time. Powerful spellcasters can draw them from the Dimension of Time via rare rituals, but doing so attracts the hounds' ire, so few who traffic in such rituals live long enough to spread their knowledge. While the hounds possess great cunning and cruel intellect, they rarely INTERACT with other criaturas-other than to hunt and destroy those who have attracted their unblinking attention.

Once a hound catches scent of a mortal to hunt, it calls others of its ilk. The pack then pursues its victim through all space and time until it catches, slays and devours them. Those pursued can escape only by avoiding all angles, as hounds of Tindalos could step through them from nothingness at any time.

Minognos-Ushad.name: Minognos-Ushad
Minognos-Ushad.publicNotes:
A wyvern is a venomous drake with a well-earned reputation for impatience and aggression. As much as 15 pies long and weighing up to 1,000 pounds, a wyvern's resilient body allows it to crash talons-first into large prey without serious risk to itself. A wyvern uses its momentum to stun its target before injecting it with searing venom or carrying it over the side of a nearby cliff. Because a wyvern lacks the strength to haul its prey all the way to its nest intact, it is far more likely to lift and drop its victim over a gully or canyon and let gravity do its work before it descends to pick apart the carcass.

Conversation is of little interest to a wyvern, as the criatura typically speaks only to taunt its prey, issue territorial claims, or demand tribute. Even so, many wyverns enjoy grim humor and tales of violent acts, particularly if those acts were committed by the storyteller. A wyvern properly appeased with meat, entertainment, and treasure sometimes agrees to provide assistance ranging from giving directions to serving as a mount for a powerful humanoid. However, these arrangements rarely last more than a few weeks before the wyvern's pride, malice, or insolence inspires it to flee or even betray its allies. Only the truly cruel can cow a wyvern into servitude for an extended period, as most wyverns are so self-interested that they go out of their way to avoid helping others.

Ravenous, bestial, and driven by instinct-drakes are primitive draconic monsters who bear a fraction of the terrifying might of their larger cousins but little (if any) of the cunning. While they're weaker, slower, and less inclined toward reason than dragons, drakes are nonetheless a menace to criaturas and settlements around them. Their propensity for forming raiding parties-small social groups fittingly called "rampages"-makes them all the more dangerous; a single rampage of river drakes can quickly lay waste to a waterside village, and roving rampages of desert drakes are a plague to caravan traders.

Drakes share a number of physical characteristics that unite them as one species despite their wide variety of habitats and abilities. For example, drakes lack forearms, leaving them only their formidable jaws and thick-scaled tails with which to attack if engaged at melee range. Most drakes would rather avoid close combat, however, preferring to use their breath armas to wreak havoc in wide swaths from comfortable distances while flying overhead. Finally, all drakes have small reservoirs of their ancestral draconic power that they can tap into to perform incredible feats of speed.

Ngara.name: Ngara
Ngara.publicNotes:
In naga culture, the foul-tempered, unkempt spirit naga holds a contemptible place similar to that of hags in humanoid cultures. Estos decrepit criaturas live out lives of solitude, sought out only by those who are foolish or brave enough to think they can benefit from the spirit naga's powers without paying a heavy price-for most who dare to show such hubris, the price is their own lives.

Spirit nagas seek out desolate ruins and places long associated with death and corruption. Estos sinister, serpentine beings can be found in abandoned graveyards, crumbled fortresses, rotting swamps, and blighted woodlands. Though they may know little of the actual history of such places, the nagas are nonetheless attracted to the psychic remnants of evil deeds and tormented spirits that remain within the earth and stones there.

Despite their hideous appearance and treatment as pariahs by other nagas, spirit nagas feel a profound pride in their abilities and even in their hermetic existences. They see themselves as connected to a greater force whose mysteries are revealed only to those who can cast off the trappings and morals of "civilized" SOCIETY. Even so, spirit nagas gleefully accept the worship of other criaturas willing to bow to their capricious whims. They often form cults around themselves, using their charm conjuros and rituals to ensnare the minds of a few key individuals who spread the nagas' foul influence throughout a community.

Nagas are identifiable by their serpentine bodies and strange, humanlike heads. All nagas have magical abilities and great INTELLIGENCE, which they combine to advance their own agendas.

Nightmare Rook.hpDetails: regeneration 20 (desactivada por cold iron or lawful)
Nightmare Rook.publicNotes:
Legendarily massive raptors capable of carrying off elephants as prey, rocs are typically about 30 pies long from beak to tail and have a wingspan of 80 pies or more. While their beaks are hooked to rip flesh from bone, their hunting strategy involves grabbing their prey in their powerful talons and then dropping it from great heights before feeding. Este method creates a massive amount of carrion, which guarantees that rocs are followed by flocks of opportunistic scavengers, such as ravens and buzzards, who find it easy to steal bits of the larger birds' meals. Rocs, for the most part, don't mind these criaturas, which sometimes get gobbled up along with the rest of the roc's food.

Rocs usually nest among mountaintops and cliffs inaccessible to all but the bravest of terrestrial dwellers. They are long-range predators that hunt both land and sea in search for massive prey to sustain them and their young. Rocs are antisocial and lone hunters who compete with each other in fierce aerial battles to protect territory. But about once a decade, a mating couple pairs up to raise their chicks. Once the chicks are old enough to hunt on their own, the parents separate to once again engage in lone hunting.

Particularly skilled druids or rangers might capture and train a roc to serve as a flying mount or hunting companion, though examples of such an incredible feat of domestication are few and far between. The easiest way to rear a roc is to do so from the moment it hatches, since the chick imprints on the first criatura it sees. Acquiring a roc egg is by no means an easy feat, though, and is often a death sentence for the would-be egg-snatcher.

deity->Lamashtu.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.aipkJQxP4GBsTaGq]

For those who revel in the corruption of the pure or who find themselves spurned and neglected by a world that despises their differences, Lamashtu offers respite among her grotesque brood. The Mother of Monsters readily accepts mortals into her fold and has made it her goal to twist mortal life toward her abhorrent ideals. Her intervention is widely known to inflict corruptions and terrible nightmares. Ostracized individuals who share her ideals will find this intervention a boon, while others treat similar events as horrible curses.

Edicts bring power to outcasts and the downtrodden, indoctrinate children in Lamashtu's teachings, make the beautiful monstrous, reveal the corruption and flaws in all things

Anathema attempt to treat a mental illness or deformity, provide succor to Lamashtu's enemies

Areas of Concern aberrance, monsters, and nightmares

feat->Rogue's Racket.description: As tú started on the path of the rogue, tú began to develop tu own style to pursue tu illicit activities. Tu racket shapes tu rogue techniques and the way tú approach a job, while building tu reputation in the criminal underworld for a certain type of work. A client with deep pockets might even hire a team of rogues for a particular heist, each specializing in a different racket, in order to cover all the bases. Elige a rogue's racket.

For a ranged attack with a thrown melee arma, that arma must also be agile or finesse.

As tu rogue level increases, so does the number of dados de daño for tu sneak attack. Increase the number of dice by one at 5th, 11th, and 17th levels.

Numerian Adamantine Golem.name: Numerian Adamantine Golem
Numerian Adamantine Golem.publicNotes:
Crafted from a nigh-indestructible metal of great rarity, adamantine golems can't be destroyed except by the most powerful foes. CRAFTING an adamantine golem requires a quantity of adamantine so massive that collecting it usually requires mounting a mining expedition to a distant planet, the Plane of Earth, or an Outer Plane.

Crafted of base materials and then magically animated into a powerful guardian, the legendario golem is a living construct that mindlessly obeys its creator's commands-often continuing to do so for years or even centuries after its creator's death. There exist two known methods of animating a golem. The traditional method involves harvesting and implanting an elemental soul or essence within the newly crafted host statue, a procedure seen as vile and blasphemous to those who value the sanctity of the soul; evil or amoral golem crafters tend to prefer this method. The other, less disreputable technique involves siphoning pure vitality energy into the statue to artificially imitate the creation of a soul. The result does not give the golem a true soul and is generally a more costly and time-consuming method of creation. Regardless of the method used, the resulting golem functions the same. A golem's unique animating force leaves it susceptible to certain forms of magic, but apart from these few weaknesses, it is impervious to magic and difficult to daño with armas.

Golems work best in play as foes to vanquish rather than allies to accompany player characters on adventures. The process of creating a golem is time-consuming, expensive, and difficult, and only the most talented spellcasters or artisans can even hope to accomplish such an undertaking. While certain magical texts-so-called "golem manuals"-are said to aid golems crafters, for the most part the creation of a golem should be something left in the hands of the Game Master.

Golems have components that can be harvested as trophies or magical components; the value depends on the golem in question. Examples of components that can be harvested from golems are listed in the sidebars.

A golem is immune to conjuros and magical abilities other than its own, but each type of golem is affected by a few types of magic in special ways. Estos exceptions are listed in shortened form in the golem's stat block, with the full rules appearing here. If an entry lists multiple types (such as "cold and water"), either type of conjuro can affect the golem.

  • Harmed By Any magic of this type that targets the golem causes it to take the listed amount of daño (this daño has no type) instead of the usual effect. If the golem starts its turn in an area of magic of this type or is affected by a persistent effect of the appropriate type, it takes the daño listed in the parenthetical.
  • Healed By Any magic of this type that targets the golem makes the golem lose the ralentizado condition and gain HP equal to half the daño the conjuro would have dealt. If the golem starts its turn in an area of this type of magic, it gains the HP listed in the parenthetical.
  • Slowed By Any magic of this type that targets the golem causes it to be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Lentificado 1} for [[/br 2d6 #rounds]]{2d6 rounds} instead of the usual effect. If the golem starts its turn in an area of this type of magic, it's ralentizado 1 for that round.
  • Vulnerable To Each golem is vulnerable to one or more specific conjuros, with the effects described in its stat block.

action->Numerian Construct.description:
Any encounters with adamantine golems, guthallaths, or radiant wardens in Numeria are with ancient robotic versions of these criaturas. In encounters with them, describe them as having more technological aspects. The guthallath's erosion aura could be caused by clouds of deconstructor nanites and its annihilation beams manifest as plasma blasts. The adamantine golem might have tank treads instead of legs and its vent ability might manifest as a spray of dozens of laser beams in a cone. And the radiant warden's radiant beams and blast serve as rippling attacks of focused graviton beams.

All of these constructs have weakness 15 to critical hits and electricity, but their other statistics do not change. If tú'd rather not introduce Numeria's themes of super-science and strange technology, puedes either present these constructs as standard versions, or re-roll tu encounter to get a more appropriate result for tu game.

Once it has more than 30 HP, it can use any type of action and can use reactions, though it remains ralentizado 1 and can't take any reactions until the start of its next turn.

If a impacto crítico with an adamantine @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.6xaxxKfvXED6LfIY]{Vorpal} arma reduces the golem to 0 HP, or if such a arma hits it while it's already at 0 HP, then the golem is destroyed.

Numerian Guthallah.name: Numerian Guthallah
Numerian Guthallah.publicNotes:
A guthallath is an enormous construct created long ago by some unknown empire, probably as a war machine. Nearly 100 pies tall, this massive stone statue typically resembles a stalwart warrior wearing only a loincloth and skullcap. Few have seen the entire body of a guthallath, though; most of the time such a relic is buried up to its neck, covered in moss and stranded in some forgotten place. Yet, every so often, one of these harbingers of destruction reactivates in response to some unknown stimulus or rallying call, and when this happens, woe be unto any who stand in its way.

While the guthallath's ancient enemies are gone, it is an engine of pure destruction, designed to rampage for weeks or even months. While not intelligent enough to enjoy or regret its acts, the guthallath cannot be reasoned with-it is unaffected by most magic, and is unpredictable in how it selects its targets (and criaturas it spares).

The enigmatic and strange radiant wardens were constructed thousands of years ago to protect observatories and scholars against the incursion of alien aggressors from the Dominion of the Black. Over time, their roles as guardians expanded to include watching over any region where the laws of time and space have worn thin, particularly near portals and permanent gates between planets, planes, or dimensions.

Nyrissa.name: Nyrissa
Nyrissa.languages: hablar con animales; hablar con plantas
Nyrissa.publicNotes:
Nyrissa tiene no always been un power en el First World, but cuando ella fell en love con Count Ranalc, one de el realm's Eldest, ella challenged su place en el plane's hierarchy. El lovers inspired cada otro a increasing acts de audacity, y ello wasn't long before Nyrissa began a think de herself as el newest de el Eldest y proclaimed este a cualquier who would listen, beginning a build su own nation en el First World. Another de el Eldest, el Lantern King, saw opportunity for mayhem here. He spread su influence among su fellow demigods, y before long, several among el Eldest opposed Nyrissa's claim y took da pasos a challenge su. First, ellos sent un jabberwock a destruir su, but Nyrissa defeated ello y used su sangre a create menor jabberwocks under su own control. Then ellos attempted a rally un thousand powerful fey against su, but Nyrissa convinced those fey a serve su instead en return for un place en su domain. Finally, el Eldest exiled Count Ranalc a el Shadow Plane for helping a cause el problem en el first place. Suddenly, Nyrissa found herself sin un aliado among el Eldest. Having expended much de su energy y resources a defeat el jabberwock y recruit el thousand, ella knew que ella had lost el war y surrendered, apologizing for su acts.

El Lantern King decided que Nyrissa's apology would suffice solo for el jabberwock's death; for su otro deeds, el demanded un further punishment- Nyrissa's capacity a love. Without love, el Lantern King argued a el otro Eldest, Nyrissa would no be able a sway another de them a su side. However, si ella could replace el "thousand fey breaths" ella stole de el First World con un thousand stolen nations, ellos would accept su apology for su otro actions y restore su capacity a love. Faced con no real option, Nyrissa agreed. She fue allowed a keep su domain, now known as Thousandbreaths, but ello fue carved off a form su own demiplane a serve as un sort de prison. Her love fue taken de su y transformed into el sword Briar, que fue then entrusted a el Lantern King for safekeeping. He gifted Nyrissa con un chalice el called el Apology, un artifact capable de transforming Material Plane kingdoms ella conquered into motes de sand. Once el Apology held un thousand motes de sand, those lands would be absorbed into el First World, Nyrissa would be forgiven, y love would be restored a su.

El matter settled, el Eldest quickly moved en con su own inscrutable agendas. Yet mientras ellos eventually forget about what ellos'd done a Nyrissa, el nymph herself did no. She grew more y more obsessed con su loss de love-o perhaps ello fue el loss de love que caused su a grow more violent y obsessed. In su early attempts a discover el location de Briar, ella received el visions que would come a haunt su-que Briar would be returned a su, but solo as un instrument de su own death.

Now ella tiene but one kingdom left a claim: el nuevo kingdom risen en el Stolen Lands. With el War de el River Kings over y one kingdom un victor, el time es right for el final grain a be added a el Apology. That este va a destruir un significant region en Golarion es irrelevant a el loveless nymph; en su obsession, ella fails a see que este act puede be el very thing que drives su enemigos de a slay su as en el vision.

equipment->Ring of Energy Resistance (Ma.name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.zyAzx6fLsPurRFQO]
Ring of Energy Resistance (Major) (Fire)
equipment->Ring of Energy Resistance (Ma.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.zyAzx6fLsPurRFQO]

Este ring grants tú resistance 15 against one type of daño de energía: acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic. Each ring is crafted to protect against a particular type of daño de energía, and its design usually embodies the type of energy it protects the wearer from in some way. For instance, a ring of fire resistance might be capped with a ruby, whereas a ring of cold resistance features a sapphire instead.

action->Shame.name: Shame
action->Shame.description: Nyrissa es focused en su goal a conquer el final kingdom ella promised el Lantern King, but ella still suffers de shame cuando ella ataques anyone who wields Briar o cualquier character who rules un kingdom (particularly, cualquier PJ who serves as Ruler). @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.adventure-specific-actions.Item.764EVGVADrDSbdqu]{Forgive Foe} puede be attempted against Nyrissa con un @Check[diplomacy|dc:51] prueba o @Check[performance|dc:51] prueba. Si Nyrissa es affected by un critical success de Forgive Foe, ella calls for un truce a speak a el PJ.

action->Wild Empathy.name: Wild Empathy
action->Wild Empathy.description: Nyrissa can use DIPLOMACY to [[/act make-an-impression]] on and make very simple [[/act request]]{Requests} of animals and plant criaturas.

action->Blinding Beauty.name: Belleza cegadora
action->Blinding Beauty.description: 30 pies. Las criaturas that start their turn in the aura must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:43] salvación or be permanently @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Cegado} (plus @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Aturdido 3} on a critical failure).

action->Evasion.name: Evasión
action->Evasion.description: Cuando Nyrissa rolls un success en un salvacion de Reflejos, ella gets un exito critico en su lugar.

action->Protection from Decapitation.name: Protection from Decapitation
action->Protection from Decapitation.description: The first time Nyrissa is decapitated by any effect (including a vorpal arma like Briar), the effect is negated. She takes no daño from the attack and is not decapitated, but she then loses her protection from decapitation for 24 horas.

action->Change Shape.name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.eXleBXdAemiEoHA8]
Cambiar de forma

action->Contingency.name: Contingencia
action->Contingency.description:
Desencadenante Nyrissa is damaged by a melee strike

Efecto @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.WPXzPl7YbMEIGWfi]{Mislead} activates on Nyrissa.

action->Focus Beauty.name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.SEmSk1INZDmeoB5R]
Focus Beauty
action->Focus Beauty.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.SEmSk1INZDmeoB5R]

Nyrissa focuses her beauty upon a target within her blinding beauty aura. The criatura takes @Damage[6d12[mental]] daño (@Check[will|dc:46|basic]) and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Cegado} until the end of their next turn (@Damage[12d12[mental]] daño and permanent blindness on a critical failure). Nyrissa can Focus Beauty on a given criatura only once per turn.

action->Inspiration.name: Inspiration
action->Inspiration.description: Nyrissa can inspire an intelligent, willing criatura by scratching that criatura with a thorn from her body. Este reduces that criatura's Puntos de Golpe by 1 permanently, but grants the criatura several abilities: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.qCCLZhnp2HhP3Ex6]{Darkvision}, the ability to see @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} criaturas, and an ability boost to an ability of Nyrissa's choice. A bard granted this inspiration gains a +2 bonificador de estado to PERFORMANCE when determining the effect of compositions. Only one criatura at a time can benefit from this inspiration. For the bulk of this Adventure Path, King Irovetti carries this inspiration, but once he is slain or defeated, who Nyrissa grants the bonus to instead (if anyone) is left to the GM to determine.

action->Quickened Casting.name: Lanzamiento apresurado
action->Quickened Casting.description:
Frecuencia tres veces al día;

Requisito Nyrissa hasn't used Quickened Casting since the start of her previous turn

Efecto If Nyrissa's next action is to cast an arcane spontaneous conjuro that is 8th level or lower, reduce the number of actions to cast it by 1 (minimum 1 action).

action->Switch Fables.name: Switch Fables
action->Switch Fables.description:
Requisito Nyrissa is located in the twenty-pies diameter central area of one of the four Fables (areas M7a- M7d of the House at the Edge of Time)

Frecuencia una vez por minuto

Efecto Nyrissa Strides a minimum distance of ten pies, after which the reality of the demiplane folds around her in a tangle of vines and flowers. She then teleports from her current Fable to one of the other three of her choice, appearing in a square of her choosing within the central twenty pies of the chosen Fable.

Nyrissa's Tempest.name: Nyrissa's Tempest
Nyrissa's Tempest.description: Sudden dark clouds gather en el sky above, y moments later, blasts de lightning y swirling tornadoes begin a rip el landscape apart.
Nyrissa's Tempest.disable: @Check[nature|dc:42] (maestro) to note the magical NATURE of the storm and to perform a quick ritual and prayer to the fey spirits of the region to cause the tempest to disperse, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (9th rank, counteract DC 36) to counteract the tempest immediately.
Nyrissa's Tempest.routine:
(4 actions) If the PCs successfully sought shelter with a SURVIVAL check, the storm takes no actions if the GM fails a @Check[flat|dc:16]. Otherwise, the storm takes four of the following actions, each determined by rolling a [[/br 1d4]], during the round. On each successive round, the number of actions the storm takes is reduced by 1; when the storm is reduced to 0 actions in this way, the hazard ends.

  • 1 Thunderclap A blast of sound rips through the region. Unsheltered armies must attempt a DC 30 Morale check or increase their shaken value by 1. Unsheltered PCs take @Damage[10d6[sonic]] daño (@Check[fortitude|dc:38|basic]).
  • 2 Lightning The tempest takes its Raging Storm reaction as a single action.
  • 3 Tornado A tornado funnel extends down from the storm to unerringly strike at a PC, who must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:38] salvación.

Éxito crítico The PC escapes unscathed.

Éxito The PC is knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Tumbado} and takes @Damage[8d6[bludgeoning]] daño.

Fallo The PC is hurled through the air, taking @Damage[8d6[bludgeoning]] daño and then falling 1d6×10 pies for appropriate falling daño, landing prone.

Fallo crítico As failure, but @Damage[8d6[bludgeoning]] daño and a fall of [[/r 10*(2d8) #Feet Fallen]]{2d8 x 10 pies}.

  • 4 Renewal Blasts of wind tear through the area but do no real daño. Attempt a @Check[flat|dc:11]; on a success, the number of actions the storm takes next round is not reduced as usual.

action->Raging Storm.name: Raging Storm
action->Raging Storm.description:
Desencadenante The PCs fail an attempt to Disable the tempest, or 10 minutos pass without any attempt to leave the area (whichever comes first)

Efecto Bolts of lightning lance down from above. If the PCs managed to succeed at a SURVIVAL check to prepare for the storm, their armies are protected and only one PC (determined randomly) is targeted by this bolt, otherwise all PCs and armies are targeted by bolts. Against PCs, the bolt inflicts @Damage[10d6[electricity]] daño (@Check[reflex|dc:38|basic]). Against armies, the bolt inflicts 1 point of daño (DC 30 Mobility check negates). Then, whether or not the PCs managed to take shelter, roll initiative for Nyrissa's Tempest.

Old Crackjaw.name: Old Crackjaw
Old Crackjaw.publicNotes: Snapping turtles are freshwater reptiles with a long flexible neck, a sharp piercing beak, and a confrontational temperament that doesn't prevent some spellcasters from choosing these criaturas as familiars. They weigh about 20 pounds and have shells around 18 inches in length.

action->Deep Breath.name: Contener La Respiración
action->Deep Breath.description: Old Crackjaw puede contener la respiracion durante 30 minutos.

action->Clench Jaws.name: Clench Jaws
action->Clench Jaws.description:
Requisitos Old Crackjaw damaged a criatura with a jaws Golpe in its previous action

Efecto Old Crackjaw clenches its jaws down and automatically deals an additional @Damage[2d8[bludgeoning]] daño to the criatura it just bit.

action->Gnawing Bite.name: Gnawing Bite
action->Gnawing Bite.description: Old Crackjaw makes a jaws Golpe against an object. Este counts as two attacks when calculating Old Crackjaw's multiple attack penalización. If this Golpe hits, Old Crackjaw deals an extra die of daño del arma to the object.

action->Shell Defense.name: Shell Defense
action->Shell Defense.description: Old Crackjaw retracts its limbs and head into its shell and ends its turn. Este increases its AC to 25, but it can't act except to reemerge, which it can do as a single action.

armor->Padded Armor.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.zBYEU9E7034ENCmh]

Este armor is simply a layer of heavy, quilted cloth, but it is sometimes used because it's so inexpensive. Padded armor is easier to daño and destroy than other types of armor. Heavy armor comes with a padded armor undercoat included in its Price, though it loses the comfort rasgo when worn under heavy armor. Puedes wear just that padded armor or undercoat to sleep in, if tu heavy armor is destroyed, or when otherwise not wearing the full heavy armor. Este allows tú to keep the armor invested and benefit from the power of any runes on the associated heavy armor, but no one else can wear tu heavy armor without the padded undercoat.

equipment->Carpenter's Tools.name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.y34yjumCFakrbtdw]
Carpenter's Tools
equipment->Carpenter's Tools.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.y34yjumCFakrbtdw]

Necesitas these tools to create items from raw materials with the Craft skill. Different sets are needed for different work, as determined by the GM; for example, blacksmith's tools differ from woodworker's tools.

equipment->Repair Kit.name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.vLGDUFrg4yGzpTQX]

equipment->Repair Kit.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.vLGDUFrg4yGzpTQX]

A REPAIR kit allows tú to perform simple repairs while traveling. It contains a portable anvil, tongs, woodworking tools, a whetstone, and oils for conditioning leather and wood. Puedes use a REPAIR kit to REPAIR items using the CRAFTING skill.

Orb Blast Trap.name: Orb Blast Trap
Orb Blast Trap.description: Five globes shoot bolts of force up and down the hall when a second criatura reaches its midpoint.
Orb Blast Trap.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:48] (maestro) to deactivate the trap entirely before it triggers, @Check[thievery|dc:45] (experto) to deactivate one of the glimmering orbs after the trap rolls initiative, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (9th rank; counteract DC 41) to deactivate the trap entirely.
Orb Blast Trap.reset: La trampa deactivates 1 asalto after it has no criaturas to target and resets automatically after 1 minuto.
Orb Blast Trap.routine: (5 actions) Five energized orbs each take one action to make a force bolt attack against a different target in the hallway (a single target cannot be fired at more than una vez por asalto by the trap). La trampa doesn't take multiple attack penalties. Each orb that is disabled or destroyed reduces the trap's actions by 1.
Orb Blast Trap.stealth: (maestro) to realize that the glimmering orbs signal a dangerous trap.

action->Slam Doors.name: Slam Doors
action->Slam Doors.description:
Desencadenante A second criatura crosses a magical sensor at the midpoint of the hall.

Efecto The doors at either end of the hall slam shut and lock in place while the trap is active (the doors open automatically if the trap is disabled or destroyed). The doors (Hardness 14, HP 56 [28 BT]) can be Forced Open with a @Check[athletics|dc:40|traits:action:force-open] check, or via a @Check[thievery|dc:35|traits:action:pick-a-lock] check to Pick the Lock. La trampa rolls initiative.

Overgrown Viper Vine.name: Overgrown Viper Vine
Overgrown Viper Vine.publicNotes:
A voracious, flesh-eating carnivore, the viper vine has a single enormous blossom arising from a thick, leafy tangle of snake-like vines. When the plant senses the approach of suitable prey through its sensitive, shallowly buried root system, it rises up like an agitated snake and unfurls its brightly colored bloom, an act that releases a cloud of mind-numbing pollen. Persistent stories claim the viper vine can lure prey into its clutches by swaying with a hypnotic motion, but this effect is in fact created by this invisible, odorless pollen cloud.

Since a viper vine gains nourishment by consuming criaturas rather than through ingesting moisture and soil, it has developed rudimentary locomotion and can drag itself along the ground with its tentacle-like roots. It even has a form of rudimentary sentience, allowing it to not only discern differences in prey and make limited tactical decisions, but also to avoid criaturas that are particularly large or dangerous-looking.

The area around viper vine hunting grounds is often strewn with the partially devoured remains of victims. It's not unusual to find the rotting corpses of wild animals, ill-fated adventurers, and even giants in the plant's immediate vicinity, along with a scattering of incidental treasure left behind on the corpses. A viper vine rarely returns to the carcass of a criatura it killed earlier, preferring to hunt fresh meat.
Overgrown Viper Vine.senses: tremorsense es preciso en area A7

action->Tremorsense (Precise in Area A7,.name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.j2wsK6IsW5yMW1jW]
Tremorsense (Precise in Area A7, Otherwise Imprecise) 60 pies

action->Cold Vulnerability.name: Cold Vulnerability
action->Cold Vulnerability.description: When exposed to a cold effect, the viper vine is overwhelmed by lethargy, becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Lentificado 1} for [[/br 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Captivating Pollen.name: Captivating Pollen
action->Captivating Pollen.description:
The viper vine releases a @Template[emanation|distance:60] of invisible pollen that stays in the air for 5 asaltos unless dispersed by a moderate or stronger wind. Each criatura that enters or starts its turn in the area must attempt a @Check[will|dc:33] salvación or be captivated.

The viper vine can't use Captivating Pollen for [[/br 1d4 #Recharge Captivating Pollen]]{1d4 rounds}.

Éxito crítico The criatura is unaffected and is temporarily immune to Captivating Pollen for 24 horas.

Éxito The criatura is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Indispuesto 1}.

Fallo The criatura is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinado}, and it must spend each of its actions to move closer to the viper vine as expediently as possible while avoiding obvious dangers. If a captivated criatura is adjacent to the viper vine, it stays still and doesn't act. It ceases to be fascinated if it's no longer in the pollen aura at the end of its turn.

Fallo crítico As failure, plus the criatura is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Anonadado 2} for 24 horas.

action->Constrict.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.g26YiEIfSHCpLocV]

@Damage[(3d8+8)[bludgeoning]] daño, @Check[fortitude|dc:35|basic]

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.Constrict]

action->Grasping Roots.name: Grasping Roots
action->Grasping Roots.description:
Desencadenante a criatura attempts a Move action in area A7

Requisitos the overgrown viper vine is in area A7

Efecto The viper vine manipulates its roots to cause foliage around the triggering criatura to suddenly seem to spring to life. The triggering criatura must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:35] tirada de salvación.

Éxito crítico El objetivo is unaffected.

Éxito El objetivo treats the first square of its movement as difficult terrain.

Fallo El objetivo becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Inmovilizado} by the foliage, (escape DC 35).

Fallo crítico As failure but el objetivo also falls @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Tumbado}.

Oversized Chimera.name: Oversized Chimera
Oversized Chimera.publicNotes: The chimera is the archetypal example of an unnatural monster made up of a monstrous mix of wildly different component criaturas: in this case, a lion, a dragon, and a goat. Wild, hateful, and hungry, it tries to eat any criatura it sees, but sometimes a strong-willed maestro is able to compel a chimera to serve as a guardian or even a mount.

action->Three Headed.name: Three Headed
action->Three Headed.description: Any ability that would sever a chimera's head (such as a impacto crítico with a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.6xaxxKfvXED6LfIY]{Vorpal Weapon}) severs one head at random. Losing a head doesn't kill a chimera (as long as it has one head left), but it does prevent it from making Golpes with the lost head or using the head's Breath Weapon.

action->Triple Opportunity.name: Triple Opportunity
action->Triple Opportunity.description: Un oversized chimera obtiene 2 reacciones adicionales cada asalto que ello puede usar solo a make ataques de Opportunity. It debe usar un diferente cabeza for cada reaction, y ello puede't usar more than one en el mismo triggering action. Si ello pierde one de su cabezas, ello also pierde one de these reacciones adicionales.

action->Breath Weapon.name: Arma de aliento
action->Breath Weapon.description:
The oversized chimera breathes a @Template[cone|distance:30] of fire that deals @Damage[13d6[fire]|options:area-damage] daño to all criaturas in the area (@Check[reflex|dc:32|basic|options:area-effect] salvación).

The chimera can't use Breath Weapon again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Breath Weapon]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Draconic Bite.name: Draconic Bite
action->Draconic Bite.description: An oversized chimera's dragon head deals an extra @Damage[3d6[fire]] daño (already included).

action->Three-Headed Strike.name: Three-Headed Golpe
action->Three-Headed Strike.description: The oversized chimera makes a Golpe with its dragon jaws, lion jaws, and goat horns, each at a -2 penalización and targeting a different criatura. Estos Golpes count as only one attack for the chimera's multiple attack penalización, and the penalización doesn't increase until after it has made all three attacks.

Paranoia Well.name: Paranoia Well
Paranoia Well.description: Sudden invasive emotions de fear, paranoia, y anger well up en el mind, causing companions a reciben en sinister casts a su no-longer familiar features.
Paranoia Well.disable: @Check[intimidation|dc:47] (legendario) to shout down the emotional energies and exert mental dominance over them, or @Check[thievery|dc:44] (maestro) to cause the trap's energies to discharge harmlessly

action->Reveal the Enemy.name: Reveal the Enemy
action->Reveal the Enemy.description:
Desencadenante A Small or larger criatura ends its turn inside of area B7

Efecto La trampa releases its built-up emotional energy in a silent blast of power. All criaturas in area B7 or within 20 pies of the shed's exterior walls must attempt a @Check[will|dc:41] salvación (criaturas within the shed take a -2 penalización de circunstancia to this save).

Éxito crítico The criatura is unaffected.

Éxito For 1 hora, the criatura treats no other criaturas as allies and can't take concentrate actions that don't have the rage rasgo.

Fallo As success, but the effect is permanent.

Fallo crítico As failure, but the criatura must attack any criatura it detects, preferring to attack former friends or allies when possible.

action->Vengeful Rage.name: Vengeful Rage
action->Vengeful Rage.description:
Desencadenante Jewel is either killed or knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Inconsciente}

Efecto Pavetta flies into a rage. She gains 20 Puntos de Golpe temporales, gains a +4 bonificador de circunstancia on tiradas de ataque, and deals 4d6 daño adicional with melee armas. In addition, she becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confundido}. Este rage persists for 1 minuto or until she ceases to be confused, after which she becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigado}.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feat-effects.Item.z3uyCMBddrPK5umr]{Efecto: Rage}

action->Baroness's Scream.name: Baroness's Scream
action->Baroness's Scream.description: Pavetta attempts a single INTIMIDATION check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2u915NdUyQan6uKF]{DEMORALIZE} and applies the result to every opponent within @Template[emanation|distance:30]{30 pies}. Additionally, she automatically alerts any allies within 100 pies that are able to hear her to her need for assistance. The baroness can't Scream for 1 asalto.

action->Release Jewel.name: Release Jewel
action->Release Jewel.description: With un command a Jewel, Pavetta releases su a serve as un minion. She debe concentrate a sustain este ability, during que ella continues a shout commands a el little dog.

action->Stabbing Fit.name: Stabbing Fit
action->Stabbing Fit.description:
Requisito Pavetta is affected by Vengeful Rage.

Efecto Pavetta makes up to five melee Golpes with her dagger, each against a different target. Estos attacks count toward her multiple attack penalización, but the penalización doesn't increase until after she makes all of her attacks.

Phantasmagoric Fog Trap.name: Phantasmagoric Fog Trap
Phantasmagoric Fog Trap.description: Cloying violet mist billows from the undergrowth, filling the heads of any criaturas inside with maddening visions of dark moonless nights, twisted malignant trees, and steaming rivers of blood.
Phantasmagoric Fog Trap.disable: @Check[survival|dc:28] (experto) to find a path through the Grand Hall that doesn't disturb the undergrowth

action->Blow Mists.name: Blow Mists
action->Blow Mists.description:
Desencadenante A criatura moves through the undergrowth

Efecto One round later, the hall fills with violet fog that imposes a -2 penalización de circunstancia to Perception checks to all criaturas within it and exposes anyone who enters it to phantasmagoric fog.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.zGWc4q0rXW9eMoYT]{Efecto: Phantasmagoric Fog}

action->Phantasmagoric Fog.name: Phantasmagoric Fog
action->Phantasmagoric Fog.description:
Tirada de salvación @Check[will|dc:24]

Duración máxima 6 asaltos

Etapa 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Anonadado 1} (1 asalto)

Etapa 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confundido} and stupefied 1 (1 asalto)

Etapa 3 confused and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Anonadado 2} (1 asalto).

action->Thematic Action - Ally.name: Thematic Action - Ally
action->Thematic Action - Ally.description: The protagonist takes the form of a recognizable support character. Its thematic action is to grant an adjacent criatura 4d4 Puntos de Golpe temporales, which last for 1 asalto.

Phomandala.name: Phomandala
Phomandala.publicNotes:
Monstrous humanoids that resemble humans with snakes instead of hair, medusas are best known for their petrifying gazes that-if lingered upon-can permanently transform mortals to stone. Medusas are shrewd and manipulative adversaries who collect and covet secrets, and who use threats and guile to exploit the fears of weaker criaturas. A medusa may seek out powerful magic items, use divination magic to discover secret knowledge and unlock forbidden power, or infiltrate a SOCIETY to beguile influential politicians. Their ability to worm their way into powerful organizations makes them natural leaders of criminal outfits and thieves' guilds, and their interest in magical phenomena leads some to pursue careers as oracles who offer to help adventurers find what they seek-for a price. Of course, if wit and DECEPTION proves insufficient, a medusa can always simply turn rivals into ornate stone decorations with little more than a glare.

Exceptionally agile and surprisingly hardy, a medusa rarely backs down from a conflict even when cornered. Many adventurers who thought themselves readied to resist the effects of a medusa's gaze have nevertheless fallen to a medusa, as these criaturas are also often deadly archers able to riddle their foes with venom-coated arrows from a distance. Still, a medusa may barter for their life if no alternatives remain, and the secrets carried by these powerful villains often make it more than worth sparing the monster's life.

Prank Workshop Mitflit.name: Prank Workshop Mitflit
Prank Workshop Mitflit.publicNotes:
Mitflits, also known as mites, are self-loathing and pitiful cowards, easily bullied into servitude by other criaturas or even slightly more powerful mitflit leaders. They tame insects, spiders, and other such criaturas to serve as faithful allies. Mitflits have lost most of their ancestral gremlin magic, leaving these incomplete beings full of doubt and insecurity. Mitflits find companionship in the other base criaturas of the world, and forge bonds of friendship with vermin, the only other beings that seem willing to accept them. A social structure, even one in which they are bullied, partially fills the hole within mitflits' personalities, and they rarely rebel or rail out unless their rage hits a breaking point.

Gremlins are cruel fey tricksters and saboteurs who have fully acclimated to life on the Material Plane, finding distinct niches for their inventive destructiveness. All gremlins delight in ruining or breaking things, whether it's something physical like a device or vehicle or something intangible such as an alliance or relationship. A gremlin's greatest joy is watching the collapse of complex creations, preferably after the lightest and slightest, carefully targeted push from the gremlin. Gremlins tend to denigrate, bully, or even slaughter their lesser kin, particularly mitflits, whom gremlins (and many others) derisively call "mites."

Rezatha.name: Rezatha
Rezatha.publicNotes:
A remorhaz is an enormous arctic predator that resembles a multilegged insect with draconic features. Este monster has chitinous plates and more than a score segmented legs, a multipartite maw, and winglike growths fianking its head. The most unusual aspect of the criatura, however, is its internal heat, which burns with such intensity that it causes the armored plates on the criatura's back to become superheated siempre que the beast is agitated.

Remorhazes are carnivores. Their diet includes arctic animals such as elk, but a hungry remorhaz readily devours anything it can catch and kill. It commonly lurks beneath ice or snow and ambushes prey with a sudden upward strike. Many victims die before even knowing what attacked them.

Those who survive the worm's initial onslaught must face not only its deadly jaws, but also its hideously hot body. Este heat can melt armas, scorch armor, and burn flesh-all tactics the remorhaz uses to disable and defeat its foes. A remorhaz's internal fire allows it to burrow through ice and snow with ease. It leaves smooth tunnels in its wake as melted ice refreezes to leave the telltale signs of its passage. Most people underestimate a remorhaz's INTELLIGENCE, assuming it to be a mere animal. However, remorhazes are capable of learning languages. Frost giants in particular use this rasgo to form alliances with them. The giants provide food, protection, and shelter for the worm, and in return the remorhaz acts as a guard beast and helps the giants build fortresses and forge metal armas. The giants also employ the worms as war beasts, using them to undermine enemigo positions.

Rigg Gargadilly.name: Rigg Gargadilly
Rigg Gargadilly.publicNotes:
Few criaturas can match a quickling's speed. Estos malicious fey criaturas delight in striking with blinding speed and accuracy, racing in to stab and slash at foes before scampering away for cover with maddening- even frightening-swiftness. Stories of people simply doubling over, bleeding from what appear to be spontaneously opening wounds, are often eyewitness accounts of quickling attacks.

Quicklings actively hate the "slow-paced dullards" they encounter every day, delighting in inflicting suffering and pain on criaturas they deem too sluggish to matter. While they are related to kinder fey such as brownies and pixies, quicklings care only for their own merriment. They see their own cruel pranks as the height of humor and have full confidence that their speed and invisibility will keep them safe from harm. They occasionally form gangs of up to a dozen individuals, although the group usually devolves very quickly into mayhem, as they inevitably perform increasingly deadly pranks against each other.

Risen Fetch.name: Risen Fetch
Risen Fetch.publicNotes:
Echoes of the corrupted soul of the undead can be used to spawn a fetch as well. A risen fetch appears more as its source did in life than as an undead.

A fetch is a twisted, deviant simulacrum of a humanoid criatura that exists or existed at one point on the Material Plane. Rumors of fetches that are reflections of entities from other planes persist, but none of these tales speak of fetches that duplicate anything other than a sapient source. A fetch can manifest spontaneously when a powerful criatura undergoes a significant emotional event or dies, either while on the First World or while in an area significantly influenced by the First World, but one can also be created by significant forces like the Eldest in order to torment and vex those who have annoyed them. While a fetch manifests from a soul's "reflection," and as such bears a striking resemblance to that criatura's appearance in life, a fetch has no true memories of its own. It keeps fragments of false remembrances from its source as if it experienced them in a half-remembered dream-which ensure the fetch is enraged by and jealous of its source.

A fetch is similar in appearance to the criatura whose soul spawned it, save that it often displays fey-like features such as pointed ears, plantlike elements, or supernatural grace. A fetch who seeks to impersonate a stillliving source must disguise these features, and takes care to manifest its fetch arma as one known to be wielded by its target.

When a fetch dies, it and its manifested items fades away into a bloom of plant life, its soul instantly recycled into the First World, leaving behind a patch of weeds and thorny flowers roughly in the shape they held in mockery while alive.

River Elasmosaurus.name: River Elasmosaurus
River Elasmosaurus.publicNotes:
Elasmosauruses are long-necked, primeval reptiles that dwell in deep oceans and seas. Although not truly a dinosaur, elasmosauruses are often found in similar locations and are similarly titanic criaturas. Keeping their massive bodies underwater, elasmosauruses use their long necks to catch prey and snorkel air to their massive lungs while remaining mostly hidden from the surface above. An elasmosaurus is 30 pies long and weighs 6,000 pounds.

As rare and reclusive as they are, elasmosauruses are sometimes mistaken for even rarer criaturas called water orms, legendario aquatic denizens of remote lakes known for their elusiveness and craftiness. Whereas elasmosauruses are mundane criaturas of animalistic INTELLIGENCE, water orms are magical beings with near-humanoid INTELLIGENCE and a curious fascination with mortals, and they seem to delight in confounding onlookers. As a result, it's theorized that a typical water orm is more than happy to lead a group of spectators to a lost elasmosaurus, both to throw its pursuers off its tail and for the hilarity that will inevitably ensue.

While elasmosauruses are often found in lost worlds and unsettled regions, those who dwell in the oceans of the world do not contain their hunting grounds to specific regions. As a result, it's not unheard of for a wandering specimen to find its way to coastal waters. Those that do often find the ports of small towns or even large cities to be wondrous banquets and are usually hunted down by coastal guards or adventurers. When a wayward elasmosaurus like this finds its way into a city's sewer system or reservoirs, though, it can become the stuff of urban legends.

Over 3 years, the surviving boggards develops arms, legs, and lungs while learning the rudiments of hunting, crafts, and warfare-everything needed to survive in their might-makes-right SOCIETY. At the top of most boggard hierarchies lords a hulking swampseer imbued with sinister divine magic.

Shambler.name: Broza Movediza
Shambler.publicNotes:
Shamblers are cunning carnivorous plants that resemble heaps of wet, rotting vegetation. Even when standing erect on their stumpy legs, shamblers don't have much in the way of identifiable anatomy; they are tangles of parasitic vines that lash out at prey with their longest creepers, entwined together to deliver powerful blows. Sometimes called "shambling mounds," these ambush predators have a particular fondness for flesh, and are most well known for their ability to hunker down and hide in plain sight. A shambler can draw nutrients from plant matter or soil, but won't do so if it suspects meat might soon wander near, and indeed may lie in wait for days in anticipation of such a meal.

Shamblers are usually solitary criaturas. Fierce thunderstorms are among the few events that bring numerous shamblers together. During such gatherings, the plants gather around strange but seemingly sacred earthen mounds in remote jungles and swamps and cavort and caper excitedly, stretching their tendrils toward the sky to hope for-or perhaps to summon-intense lightning strikes. Not only are these strange plants unharmed by even the most powerful electrical strikes, but they seem to become supernaturally empowered by such bursts of raw energy. Shamblers consider being struck by lightning a sign of divine favor, and those shamblers frequently blasted by bolts of electricity become respected elders among their kind. Shambler elders are few and far between and may possess a wide array of abilities; some can cast primal conjuros, others can empathically call upon the aid of other shamblers in the area, and still others wield awesome powers over electricity.

Other types of shamblers exist, including those composed not of plant matter but fungal growth. Spirit of Stisshak.name: Spirit of Stisshak
Spirit of Stisshak.publicNotes:
Malevolent balls of colored light, will-o'-wisps haunt lonely marshes and forests where they lure unsuspecting travelers into danger. Will-o'-wisps can vary the color and illumination they shed, and delight in mimicking bobbing lanterns or distant fires to draw lost or disoriented travelers off of safe trails. They can extinguish their illumination entirely to become invisible, and they enjoy doing so once their victims are wholly lost and have realized that the bobbing light in the distance isn't, in fact, leading them to safety. Even invisible, however, a will-o'-wisp rarely ventures far from its target, as it feasts upon the panic and dread felt by its victims.

Beneath its glow, a will-o'-wisp's body is a spongy ball approximately 1 pies in diameter and weighing less than 5 pounds. Although most will-o'-wisps are merely translucent, featureless orbs, gaining definition only in the shifting illumination they create, a few have dark mottling that makes them resemble a skull when viewed closely. Will-o'-wisps have no need for mundane nourishment, and in fact lack the ability to consume matter of any kind; they find all the sustenance they need in the terror of nearby criaturas. For this reason, they like to work alongside undead that produce terror in their victims. Will-o'-wisps are long-lived, if not effectively immortal, and they have good memories. A cowed or defeated will-o'-wisp can be a good source of LORE and information, though acquiring such cooperation from such a sinister monster is no easy feat.

Will-o'-wisps inhabit desolate swamps and forests and are generally active at twilight and after dark. They are therefore reluctant to lead victims into immediately fatal areas such as deadfalls, but instead prefer hazards where their victims suffer over a long time, such as pockets of stale or poisonous air, patches of quicksand, and dens of bigger monsters. According to will-o'-wisps, different types of fear have subtle differences in flavor. The lurking dread in the pit of the stomach that gnaws at those who slowly become aware of the fact that they're lost produces a much different taste than the sudden stark terror of imminent death in the face of a towering monster. Because of this, will-o'-wisps try to vary the ways in which they induce terror in their prey, to ensure they don't tire of certain flavors of fear.

Storm-Struck Arboreal.name: Storm-Struck Arboreal
Storm-Struck Arboreal.publicNotes:
Arboreal regents-also called treants-are lumbering, solitary criaturas responsible for guarding an entire forest. They take an especially long view of affairs and never act brashly or without much deliberation. They occasionally come together in small groups called groves to share news and pass their wisdom down to the arboreal wardens that have sprouted under their watch. In times of grave danger, all the groves in a region may gather for a great months-long meeting to plan and, eventually, act upon a threat.

The typical arboreal regent is 30 pies tall, has a trunk 2 pies in diameter, and weighs 4,500 pounds.

Arboreals are guardians of the forest and representatives of the trees. As long-lived as the woods they watch over, arboreals consider themselves parents and shepherds of trees rather than their gardeners. Consequently, while arboreals tend to be slow and methodical, they are terrifyingly swift when forced to fight in defense of the woods. Though they rarely seek out the companionship of short-lived folk-even elves are fugacious in the eyes of arboreals-and have an inherent distrust of change, arboreals have been known to tolerate those who seek to learn from their long-winded, rambling monologues, especially if such pupils also express a desire to protect the timberlands. Against those who threaten their realm, such as loggers eager to harvest lumber or settlers aiming to establish croplands or a town, arboreals' wrath is unwavering and devastating. Perhaps ironically, arboreals are gifted at tearing down what others build-a rasgo that serves vengeful members of their kind well.
